questions.q: What is the key difference between Delete and Hard Delete in Data Loader?
options: Delete removes fields; Hard Delete removes objects
Hard Delete only works on custom objects
Delete sends records to the Recycle Bin; Hard Delete bypasses it and is permanent
There is no difference except speed
questions.explain: Regular Delete is recoverable from the Recycle Bin; Hard Delete permanently removes records.

questions.q: What must a Delete CSV file contain?
options: An Id column identifying each record to delete
The record Names only
Every field of each record
A SOQL query
questions.explain: Delete works by record Id, so the CSV needs an Id column.

questions.q: What should you do first, before deleting records in bulk?
options: Give yourself Hard Delete permission
Disable the Recycle Bin
Delete everything in one big file to save time
Export the affected records to a CSV as a backup
questions.explain: An export preserves the original data in case the delete was a mistake.

questions.q: Why rehearse a delete in a sandbox first?
options: Sandboxes delete records faster
A mistake there affects only test data, not live production data
Deletes only work in a sandbox
It skips the need for an Id column
questions.explain: A sandbox lets you confirm the file and process without real consequences.

questions.q: For roughly how long can a regular deleted record be restored from the Recycle Bin?
options: Never; deletes are always permanent
One hour
About 15 days
Exactly one year
questions.explain: Records deleted normally stay recoverable in the Recycle Bin for about 15 days.
